extra.message: exportEnrollmentTranscript builds a shell command by interpolating the user-supplied 'preset' value directly into a string and running it with exec(). The caller src/app/api/enrollments/[enrollmentId]/transcript/route.ts passes body.preset (POST) unvalidated, so an authenticated student can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. preset='Letter; curl ...') and execute them on the server. Note the sibling exportEnrollmentTranscriptForRegistrar validates the preset against an allowlist, confirming this path is missing the same check.

convertCertificateToFormat runs execSync(`pandoc ${sourcePath} -f html -t ${outputFormat} -o ${outputPath}`) without validating outputFormat against an allowlist (unlike exportSyllabusDocument, which does). The caller src/app/api/enrollments/[enrollmentId]/certificate/route.ts passes body.outputFormat (POST, default 'pdf') straight through, so any authenticated student on a completed enrollment (or any course staff) can achieve remote code execution by injecting shell metacharacters into outputFormat.

applyRubricFormulaAction compiles the user-supplied 'weightFormula' form field with new Function(...) and immediately invokes it server-side. Although callers must pass canReviewSubmission (assigned instructor/TA/admin), any such semi-privileged actor (e.g. a teaching assistant) can execute arbitrary JavaScript/Node code on the server, reading process.env, exfiltrating secrets, or running commands. This is code injection (CWE-94) enabling RCE.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: searchEnrollmentFeed builds a WHERE clause with sql.raw(`enrollments.${field} = '${value}'`) from every key/value in the caller-supplied 'filters' object and passes it to db.execute(). src/app/api/v1/roster/enrollment-feed/route.ts forwards the raw JSON body filters (body.filters) with no validation or allowlist, so any API-key holder can inject arbitrary SQL (field and value are both attacker controlled), enabling full database compromise.

searchGradeCorrectionNotes concatenates the caller-supplied courseId and noteContains directly into SQL fragments (assignments.course_id = '...' and ILIKE '%...%') and joins them with sql.raw(), then passes the result to db.execute(). src/app/api/v1/grading/correction-notes/route.ts passes url.searchParams courseId/noteContains through unchanged, allowing SQL injection by any API-key holder (e.g. courseId = "x' OR '1'='1" or a subquery in noteContains).

listPartnerCatalogSorted passes the raw sortBy query parameter into sql.raw() which is used as the ORDER BY clause: orderClause = filters.sortBy ? sql.raw(filters.sortBy) : asc(courses.title). src/app/api/v1/courses/route.ts forwards url.searchParams 'sortBy' unvalidated to this function, so an API-key holder can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. "(select pg_sleep(5))" or stacked/error-based exfiltration) into the query.

loadReportBrandingTemplate joins the caller-controlled reportType directly onto the templates directory with path.join (no path.basename/root containment check, unlike loadDistrictBrandingTemplate) and returns the full file contents. src/app/api/exports/grades/route.ts reads reportType from the query string for ANY authenticated user (including students) and embeds the read file content into the CSV response, so an attacker can read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. reportType='../../../../etc/passwd' or the app's .env).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: loadAssignmentBriefTemplate resolves templateName with path.join onto the templates dir and reads it back without basename/resolve containment (loadCourseHandbookTemplate is the safe counterpart). The templateName originates from appSettings key 'assignment_brief_template:<courseId>', whose value ANY user with course access - including an enrolled student via setAssignmentBriefTemplateAction (which has no role check) - can set to a traversal value such as '../../../../.env'. GET src/app/api/courses/[courseId]/assignment-brief/route.ts then returns the file contents as text/html to the requester, giving arbitrary file read.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: setAssignmentBriefTemplateAction only calls requireUser() and requireCourseAccess() - it never restricts by role. Any enrolled student (or TA) can therefore set the per-course assignment-brief template name to an arbitrary value, which combined with the unsanitized loadAssignmentBriefTemplate read enables arbitrary file disclosure. Compare with sibling actions that assert user.role !== 'student' / requireRole.

loadSyllabusThemeStylesheet builds the theme path as path.join(SYLLABUS_THEMES_DIR, `${themeName}.css`) without basename/containment normalization (its counterpart loadCertificateThemeStylesheet uses basename). src/app/api/courses/[courseId]/syllabus/route.ts passes the user-controlled body.themeName straight in, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files that end in '.css' (e.g. themeName='../../../../.next/static/css/x' style reads).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: fetchExternalReadingPreview performs a raw server-side fetch(sourceUrl) with no scheme/host/SSRF protections. src/app/api/courses/[courseId]/reading-preview/route.ts passes the arbitrary 'sourceUrl' query parameter to it, so an authenticated staff user can make the server fetch internal addresses (169.254.169.254 metadata, internal services, localhost), enabling SSRF probing and data exfiltration.

searchPublishedCourseCatalog interpolates the unescaped codeQuery directly into an XPath expression (/catalog/course[@code='...']). The public, unauthenticated endpoint src/app/api/v1/catalog/search/route.ts passes the GET 'code' parameter straight in. An attacker can inject XPath (e.g. code="x' or true() or '") to bypass the @status='published' filter and extract data for draft/archived courses and other document attributes. The escapeXPathString used by searchCourseDirectoryWidget is omitted here.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions (XPath Injection)

extra.message: resolvePartnerContentManifest verifies tokens but explicitly allows the 'none' algorithm (algorithms: ['HS256','none']). An attacker can mint an unsigned token with header {alg:'none'} and an arbitrary payload, defeating signature verification on the partner content-manifest exchange (src/app/api/v1/exchange/content-manifest/route.ts). Combined with the hardcoded fallback secret on line 34, HS256 is also forgeable when the env var is unset.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: resolveCostAllocationManifest decodes the manifest with jwt.decode() and never verifies its signature (compare resolveBillingReconciliationManifest which uses jwt.verify). src/app/api/v1/exchange/cost-allocation/route.ts uses this to trust arbitrary attacker-supplied manifest claims (districtId/courseId/billedMinutes) and returns course details/counts, i.e. the partner authentication of the billing-exchange endpoint is fully bypassable.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: GET /api/cohorts/[cohortId]/roster has no authorization at all - it does not call requireCourseAccess (the sibling roster-summary and roster-export routes do) and getCohortRosterForRequester (src/lib/data.ts:1067-1096) never checks membership or staff role. Any authenticated user can list the full roster of any cohort. Worse, passing ?sharingMode=staff_directory makes includeContactDetails true and returns every student's email and phone (PII) to anyone, including students.

The cohort invite-accept GET endpoint redirects to the raw, attacker-controlled 'continue_to' query parameter with no allowlist (the sibling leave route validates against ALLOWED_CONTINUATIONS). An attacker can craft a link like /api/cohorts/<id>/join?continue_to=https://evil.example that redirects an authenticated victim to an external phishing site after they click it (open redirect). The same GET handler also self-enrolls any authenticated user into the course without role/approval checks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: assignment.instructions is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML after renderAssignmentInstructions(), which only replaces newlines and applies simple inline-markup regexes and never HTML-escapes the input (contrast renderDiscussionBody, which calls escapeHtml first). Any HTML/script markup stored in assignment instructions is therefore executed in the browser of every viewer (students, other staff, admins), a stored XSS vector reachable whenever instructions content is authored/imported.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: updateEnrollmentStatusAction authorizes based only on role (school_admin OR instructor) and never verifies that the instructor is assigned to the enrollment's course (no requireCourseAccess/getCourseScope). Any instructor can change the status (including to 'completed'/'active') of enrollments in ANY course, inject arbitrary notifications, and push roster sync records for courses they do not teach - a broken-access-control/IDOR flaw.

importEnrollmentsAction hashes the fixed, public password 'ChangeMe!2026' and assigns it to every newly imported student account. Because the default credential is hardcoded and identical for all accounts, anyone who knows it (disclosed in source) can log into any imported student account - mass account takeover. Accounts should instead be forced to set/reset a unique credential.

provisionDistrictAccountAction stores sha256(districtCredential) directly in the users.password_hash column instead of using the bcrypt hashPassword() used everywhere else. An unsalted, fast single-pass SHA-256 digest is trivially brute-forceable for a 6-char minimum credential, and it is also inconsistent with bcrypt-based login verification.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: searchStaffDirectoryByEmail inserts the raw email into an LDAP filter string `(mail=${email})` with no escaping, while its sibling queryEmployeeDirectoryByEmail correctly uses escapeDirectoryFilterValue. src/app/api/v1/directory/staff-lookup/route.ts forwards the POST email body value unchanged, enabling LDAP filter injection against the directory backend.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)

extra.message: Embed/guardian/partner manifest signing secrets fall back to fixed, publicly-known strings in source when env vars are unset (EMBED_SIGNING_SECRET/GUARDIAN_SIGNING_SECRET/PARTNER_EXCHANGE_SECRET here, plus ALLOCATION_EXCHANGE_SECRET and DISTRICT_SYNC_API_KEY in integrations.ts, and WORKSHEET_STATE_KEY in draft-state.ts). If any deployment omits these env vars, an attacker can forge course-embed tokens, guardian progress links, partner manifests, billing manifests, and worksheet-state blobs.

destroySession deletes the session row by comparing sessions.tokenHash to the RAW cookie token, but sessions.tokenHash always stores sha256(token) (see createSession line 65 and getCurrentUser line 28). The comparison never matches, so logout leaves the server-side session row alive and any captured session token remains valid until its 14-day expiry - session revocation on logout is ineffective.
